description:
Redirect any Windows/MacOS TCP and UDP traffic to HTTP/Socks5 proxy

ProxyBridge is a lightweight, open-source universal proxy client (Proxifier alternative) that provides transparent proxy routing for applications on Windows and macOS. It redirects TCP and UDP traffic from specific processes through SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies, with the ability to route, block, or allow traffic on a per-application basis. ProxyBridge fully supports both TCP and UDP proxy routing and works at the system level, making it compatible with proxy-unaware applications without requiring any configuration changes.
ProxyBridge v4.2.0 (Windows)
✨ What's new
⏯️ Main switch: pause ProxyBridge without closing it (#219)
- Proxy → Enable ProxyBridge, or right-click the tray icon, switches every rule off and on again.
- While paused, new connections go out directly (proxy rules and block rules don't apply). The window title and tray tooltip show (PAUSED).
- Connections already being proxied keep working until they end.
- ProxyBridge always starts enabled; the switch isn't remembered between runs.
🔎 Search in the Proxy Rules window (#248)
- A search box at the top right filters the list as you type. A rule is shown when it contains every word you type (case-insensitive) in its name, applications, hosts, ports, protocol, action or proxy, for example chrome github.
- Ctrl+F jumps to the box, typing while the list has focus starts a search, Enter / Down go to the matching rules, Esc clears.
- Edit, Clone, Remove and the enable check boxes work on the rules you see. Move Up / Move Down are only available when no search is active.
🌐 One Target Hosts field for IPs and domains (#251)
- IP addresses, ranges and domain names now go in the same field and can be mixed: 10.*.*.*; github.com; *.google.com.
- The box is multiline, up to 8191 characters (it was about 254). One entry per line is fine; line breaks are only for readability and ; separates entries.
- A rule matches when the connection's IP matches an IP entry or its domain matches a domain entry. Before, a rule with both an IP list and a domain list needed both to match.
- A domain typed in the IP part, which used to silently match nothing, now just works.
- Profile files still save TargetHosts and TargetDomains, so profiles stay compatible with macOS, Linux and older versions.
🏠 "Also proxy localhost traffic" is now per rule
- The global Localhost via Proxy menu item is gone. Each PROXY rule has its own Also proxy localhost traffic checkbox, off by default, so one app (for example a browser) can have its 127.0.0.1 / ::1 traffic proxied while another (for example curl) keeps it direct.
- Existing profiles keep behaving the same: an old profile's global setting becomes the default for each of its rules.
🛠️ Smaller changes and fixes
- Text conversions in profile loading and saving are always properly terminated and sized for long values; a corrupt or oversized profile can no longer overflow a buffer.
- The Rules list is wider for Hosts, and the Domains column is gone (merged into Hosts).
